idiom_name: typed degraded states (discriminated union) over try/catch and Promise.allSettled
implementation_notes: The runtime mechanism is the JavaScript one - try/catch and Promise.allSettled - but TypeScript's contribution is to make the degraded quality impossible to ignore: model the result as a discriminated union (ok | degraded) so consumers must narrow before use, which is what stops stale or partial data from being treated as complete. PromiseSettledResult<T> already carries the per-dependency status, and catch parameters are unknown under useUnknownInCatchVariables, so the failure must be inspected before it is recorded. The classic mode flag becomes a variant of the return type rather than a mutable boolean.
pitfalls: catch (e) is unknown under useUnknownInCatchVariables (not any), so record or narrow it properly instead of casting to any, which re-opens the hole the union was closing.
Promise.allSettled results are positional, so a mismatched destructuring mislabels which dependency degraded (MDN documents the ordering trap).
Optional fields (value?: T) describe degraded state weakly and consumers forget to check; the discriminated union forces the branch.
